title: SNAP- and Halo-tagging and dye introduction protocol for live microscopy in Xenopus embryos
protocol: Clone the sequence of interest into the appropriate SNAPf/Halo pCS2+ vector backbone in frame without intervening stop codons.
Clone sequence of interest into the multiple cloning site (MCS) upstream or downstream of the SNAPf- or Halo-tag.
Pause point: Store DNA at −20°C for later use if necessary.
Linearize the vector using NotI or KpnI restriction enzymes.
Run linearized vector on a gel to check for proper linearization.
In vitro transcribe the linearized plasmid following SP6 mMessage mMachine kit instructions.
Purify mRNA following RNeasy kit instructions.
Run purified mRNA on a gel before experimental use to ensure expected size and purity.
Inject adult female Xenopus laevis frogs with 50 units of human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) into the dorsal lymph sac several days before egg collection.
Induce ovulation by injecting primed frogs with 400–800 units of HCG into the dorsal lymph sac on the afternoon before egg collection.
Collect eggs from adult female frogs in a petri dish filled with 1× MMR.
Remove most of the MMR, leaving approximately one-tenth of the volume remaining for fertilization.
Fertilize collected eggs with about one quarter of a testes harvested from an adult male Xenopus laevis frog.
Macerate the testes using forceps to release sperm.
Wait 1 minute and fill the dish with water to result in approximately 0.1× MMR.
Dejelly embryos at least 30 minutes post-fertilization with 2% Cysteine (in 1× MMR) adjusted to pH 7.8.
Replace media on embryos with cysteine solution, transfer embryos to a 50 mL falcon tube.
Bring the volume of cysteine solution to approximately 25 mL and gently swirl the embryos.
Pour out the cysteine once the embryos lose their jelly coating and settle at the bottom.
Rinse the embryos twice with 1× MMR and twice with 0.1× MMR.
Separate the embryos into petri dishes.
Remove any unhealthy embryos.
Incubate the embryos in 0.1× MMR until they reach a 2–4 cell stage (∼1.5–2 h post-fertilization).
Incubate dishes of embryos at 13°C, 15°C, 17°C, and room temperature (RT, 22°C) to spread the window of time embryos are at 2–4 cell stage.
Note: This range of temperatures supports normal development of Xenopus embryos.
Prepare microinjection needles by pulling 10 μL glass capillary tubes to create needles with a long, thin point.
Set up microinjector and turn on N2 tank.
Calibrate the needle.
Break the end of the needle using forceps.
Attach the needle to microinjector tubing.
Fill the needle with RNase free water.
Adjust the pressure and injection time on the microinjector so that it produces a 5 nL droplet in mineral oil.
Resuspend SNAP- or Halo-dye aliquot to an appropriate stock concentration using RNase free water.
Vortex to ensure even suspension of the dye.
Work with dyes in minimal light during resuspension and incubation.
Turn off overhead lights in the room during dye resuspension.
Keep embryos in dark incubators with tinted windows during incubation.
Mix the dye and mRNA encoding the proteins of interest to make a microinjection mix.
Mix the microinjection droplet by pipetting up and down with a micropipette to ensure an even distribution of the dye and mRNA within the droplet.
Inject 2–4 cell stage Xenopus embryos with 5 nL of the microinjection mix at two distinct locations within the animal hemisphere.
Incubate the embryos in 35 mm × 10 mm petri dishes filled with 0.1× MMR, leaving enough space so that the embryos are not crowded.
Incubate the embryos in a dark incubator at 15°C or 17°C overnight (15–22 h) for next-day imaging of embryos at gastrula stage.
Inject 2–4 cell stage Xenopus embryos with 5 nL of the microinjection mix at two distinct locations within the animal hemisphere.
Incubate the embryos microinjected with mRNA in petri dishes filled with 0.1× MMR at 17°C until dye bath is prepared in the 96-well plate.
Resuspend SNAP- or Halo-dye aliquot to working concentration using 0.1× MMR.
Add 300 μL of the resuspended dye to a single well within a 96-well plate.
Pipette thoroughly to ensure a homogeneous dye solution.
Using a transfer pipette, add 10–15 Xenopus embryos microinjected with SNAP and/or Halo mRNAs to the well.
Touch the tip of the micropipette to the surface of the dye bath when adding embryos to allow them to drop into the well without transferring additional 0.1× MMR.
Incubate the 96-well plate at 15 or 17°C overnight (15–22 h) for next-day imaging of embryos at gastrula stage.
Remove gastrula-stage Xenopus embryos from the incubator.
Select healthy embryos with even pigmentation using a dissecting microscope for live imaging.
Transfer embryos bathed in dye from the 96-well plate to a petri dish containing 0.1× MMR before viewing.
Apply a thin layer of vacuum grease to both sides of a custom metal slide with a central circular hole.
Place a square coverslip on one side of the slide, making a well.
Add three selected embryos and a small volume of 0.1× MMR to the well.
Place a second square coverslip on top of the embryos, gently sandwiching them between the two glass coverslips.
Focus on one of the embryos using a confocal microscope with a 60× objective on an inverted Olympus FV1000.
Conduct imaging as for any other fluorescently-labeled protein expressed in Xenopus embryos.
